short: Pope Pius V issued a papal bull excommunicating Queen Elizabeth I.
full:
On 25 February 1570, Pope Pius V formally promulgated the papal bull 'Regnans in Excelsis', declaring Queen Elizabeth I a usurper and heretic, and officially excommunicating her from the Catholic Church. The severe decree explicitly released all English Catholics from their earthly oaths of loyalty to the Crown and actively commanded them not to obey her laws under threat of excommunication.

The bull fundamentally and permanently altered the English political landscape, making domestic Catholicism virtually synonymous with active state treason in the eyes of the government. It triggered a much harsher legislative crackdown on religious recusants, inspired multiple international Catholic assassination plots against the queen, and solidified the hostile, existential divide between Protestant England and the Catholic powers of Europe.
